questions.stem: Which of the following is the best definition of a stakeholder?
options: Any individual or group affected by, or able to affect, the activities of a business
Any person who owns shares in a business
Any employee with a permanent contract
Any customer who has bought from the business more than once
questions.why: A stakeholder is anyone with an interest in the business, whether or not they own any part of it.
whyNot: That describes a shareholder, who is only one type of stakeholder.
Employees are stakeholders, but so are many groups outside the business.
Customers are stakeholders regardless of how often they buy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an internal stakeholder?
options: An employee
A supplier
The local community
A pressure group
questions.why: Internal stakeholders are inside the business: employees, managers and owners.
whyNot: Suppliers are outside the business, so they are external stakeholders.
The local community is external to the business.
A pressure group is an external stakeholder with no role inside the business.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines the shareholder model?
options: The view that a business should focus on maximising returns to its owners
The view that a business should consider everyone affected by its decisions
The view that employees should own shares in the business
The view that the government should regulate business objectives
questions.why: The shareholder model judges decisions by their effect on share price and dividends, because the owners bear the risk.
whyNot: That is the stakeholder model.
That is employee share ownership, which is a reward scheme rather than a model of purpose.
Regulation is an external influence, not a model of who the business is run for.

questions.stem: Which stakeholder group is most interested in prompt payment and regular orders?
options: Suppliers
Shareholders
The local community
Pressure groups
questions.why: Suppliers depend on being paid on time and on a predictable flow of orders.
whyNot: Shareholders are concerned with profit, dividends and share price.
The community is concerned with employment and local impact.
Pressure groups focus on ethical and environmental behaviour.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a criticism of the shareholder model?
options: It encourages short-termism because share price responds to quarterly results
It gives managers an objective that is too vague to measure
It makes it impossible to raise equity finance
It prevents a business from making a profit
questions.why: Because performance is judged on share price, managers face pressure to cut spending on training, maintenance and quality that only pays back later.
whyNot: Vagueness is the criticism of the stakeholder model; the shareholder model is criticised for being too narrow.
The shareholder model makes equity easier to raise, because returns are the stated priority.
It is designed to maximise profit, not prevent it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a criticism of the stakeholder model?
options: Stakeholders' objectives conflict, so managers are given a vague objective and wide discretion
It ignores the interests of employees
It is illegal in most countries
It removes the need for any objectives at all
questions.why: Because stakeholder interests genuinely conflict, telling managers to consider everyone leaves them deciding whose interests come first, which is hard to hold them accountable for.
whyNot: It explicitly includes employees; that is one of its main attractions.
It is a legitimate approach and widely adopted.
It still requires objectives; the criticism is that they are less measurable.

questions.stem: Which is the most examinable conflict between stakeholder interests?
options: Short-term profit against long-term capability
Marketing against operations
Cash against profit
Fixed costs against variable costs
questions.why: Cutting training and maintenance raises this year's profit and weakens the business later, and that time-based conflict runs through almost every stakeholder question.
whyNot: That is an internal functional issue, not a stakeholder conflict.
That is a finance distinction rather than a conflict between stakeholders.
Cost classification is a costing matter, not a stakeholder conflict.

questions.stem: In stakeholder mapping, how should a stakeholder with high power and high interest be managed?
options: Manage closely
Monitor only
Keep informed
Keep satisfied
questions.why: High power combined with high interest means the stakeholder can and will act, so they need close management.
whyNot: Monitoring is the response to low power and low interest.
Keeping informed suits low power with high interest, such as small community groups.
Keeping satisfied suits high power with low interest, such as a disengaged large investor.

questions.stem: In stakeholder mapping, a large institutional investor that currently takes little interest in the business should be:
options: Kept satisfied
Managed closely
Kept informed
Monitored only
questions.why: They have high power and low interest, so the aim is to avoid giving them a reason to become engaged.
whyNot: Close management is for those who are both powerful and already interested.
Keeping informed applies to interested stakeholders with little power.
Monitoring is for those with neither power nor interest.

questions.stem: What is the convergence argument in stakeholder theory?
options: Over a long enough horizon, treating stakeholders well is usually the route to shareholder value
All stakeholders eventually want exactly the same thing
Shareholders and managers always have identical objectives
Stakeholder interests can be measured on a single financial scale
questions.why: Mistreated employees leave, cheated suppliers withdraw credit and disappointed customers do not return, so the two models conflict mainly in the short run.
whyNot: Their objectives remain different; what converges is the outcome over time, not the wants.
The divergence between managers and shareholders is precisely why incentive schemes exist.
Many stakeholder concerns, such as reputation and morale, cannot be reduced to one financial measure.

questions.stem: A resort develops an island and considers cutting construction costs in ways that would damage the surrounding reef. Why does the convergence argument apply with unusual force?
options: The reef is the product, so damaging it destroys the asset the shareholders own
Construction costs are always a small part of total cost
Environmental groups have legal control of the business
Shareholders are not interested in long-term returns
questions.why: Where the environment is the thing customers are paying for, the environmental interest and the shareholders' long-term interest are the same, and only the short-run saving pulls the other way.
whyNot: The size of construction cost is irrelevant to whether the saving damages the asset.
Pressure groups may lobby and regulate, but they do not control the business.
Shareholders are typically very interested in long-term value; the problem is short-term pressure.

questions.stem: Why can it be misleading to say a business will consider all its stakeholders equally?
options: Stakeholders have unequal power, so in practice the powerful ones are considered most
Only shareholders are legally recognised as existing
Businesses are required by law to ignore external stakeholders
Stakeholder interests never actually conflict
questions.why: Stakeholder mapping shows who the business will actually listen to, and it is usually those with the power to act on their interest.
whyNot: Many stakeholder groups have legal rights, including employees, customers and lenders.
No such legal requirement exists.
Conflict between stakeholder objectives is the norm, not the exception.

questions.stem: A profitable business announces a large profit increase. Which combination of stakeholder reactions is most likely?
options: Shareholders pleased, unions prompted to claim higher pay, and greater government tax interest
All stakeholders equally pleased
Shareholders concerned and employees indifferent
Customers pleased and shareholders opposed
questions.why: The same figures support opposite conclusions depending on who reads them, which is a strong evaluation point.
whyNot: Stakeholders have different objectives, so a single figure does not please all of them.
Shareholders welcome higher profit, and employees are far from indifferent to it.
Shareholders are not opposed to higher profit; it is their main objective.

questions.stem: Which stakeholder group is a business's managers, and why does it matter?
options: They are internal stakeholders whose interests may diverge from those of shareholders
They are external stakeholders with no interest in performance
They are not stakeholders because they do not own shares
They are stakeholders only if they are also employees
questions.why: Managers may pursue growth or acquisitions for status rather than returns, which is the reason incentive schemes exist.
whyNot: Managers are inside the business and have a strong interest in its performance.
Ownership is not required to be a stakeholder.
All managers are stakeholders regardless of contract type.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most useful distinction to draw when judging between the two models?
options: The time horizon over which performance is judged
The legal form of the business
The size of the marketing budget
Whether the business exports
questions.why: The models conflict in the short run and largely align in the long run, so stating the horizon is what turns a list into a judgement.
whyNot: Legal form affects who the owners are but not the underlying conflict between short and long run.
The marketing budget is unrelated to the models of business purpose.
Exporting raises other issues but does not resolve the stakeholder question.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines stakeholder mapping?
options: Assessing stakeholders by their power and their level of interest in order to decide how to manage them
Listing every stakeholder a business has in alphabetical order
Calculating the financial value of each stakeholder to the business
Recording which stakeholders own shares
questions.why: The two dimensions are power and interest, and the position of each stakeholder determines the management approach.
whyNot: A list alone gives no guidance on how to handle each group.
Many stakeholder interests cannot be reduced to a financial value.
Share ownership is only one narrow aspect of stakeholder relations.
